homepage.municipality_title: A rice-growing town in Pangasinan's third district
homepage.municipality_desc: Mapandan sits in the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan, bounded by San Jacinto to the north, Mangaldan to the northwest, Manaoag to the east, and Santa Barbara to the south. Covering 30.00 square kilometres, around three-quarters of its land supports agriculture — mainly rice, alongside corn, livestock, and seasonal vegetables. The municipal administration operates under the tagline “Kaakibat niyo ang Aktibo at Responsableng Liderato” (Partnering with you in Active and Responsible Leadership).
homepage.milestone1_desc: The area belonged to Mangaldan as southern barrios — Payapay, Baloling, Apaya, and Amanoaoac — named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants along the Agno River floodplain.
homepage.milestone2_desc: Established as an independent municipality through Director General No. 39, led by ten local leaders including Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, and Andres Bongato.
homepage.milestone3_desc: A severe epidemic forced temporary re-annexation to Mangaldan due to financial insolvency. Full autonomy was restored in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith.
homepage.milestone4_desc: A 15-barangay municipality of 38,228 residents, investing in the Super Health Center, Pandan Festival, and infrastructure growth.
homepage.history_subtitle: From a new pueblo to a growing community
homepage.history_cta: Read the full history & explore historical photos →

homepage.municipality_desc_full: Mapandan sits in the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan, bounded by San Jacinto to the north, Mangaldan to the northwest, Manaoag to the east, and Santa Barbara to the south. Covering 30.00 square kilometres, around three-quarters of its land supports agriculture — mainly rice, alongside corn, livestock, and seasonal vegetables.
homepage.milestone1_era_desc: Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo through Director General No. 39, signed on December 28, 1887, separating from the town of Mangaldan.
homepage.milestone2_era_desc: After being re-annexed to Mangaldan due to financial insolvency, Mapandan regained its independence in 1909 through Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith.
homepage.milestone3_era_desc: The municipality's economy centers on rice cultivation, with irrigation systems supporting year-round farming across its lowland barangays.
homepage.history_source_desc: Historical accounts drawn from municipal archives, provincial records, and published heritage studies of Pangasinan.
homepage.pandan_desc: Held annually during the second week of April, the Pandan Festival celebrates Mapandan's cultural heritage with street dancing, pageants, and community gatherings.
homepage.plaza_desc: Located in Poblacion, the Mapandan Town Plaza serves as the civic center for public gatherings, celebrations, and community events.
homepage.agri_desc: Barangay Luyan is highlighted in regional DOT programs for its rice paddies, scenic farm routes, and community-based tourism initiatives.
homepage.founded_desc: Separated from Mangaldan as an independent pueblo under Governor General Emilio Bravo, led by ten local leaders including Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, and Andres Bongato.
homepage.reestablished_desc: A severe epidemic forced temporary re-annexation to Mangaldan. Full autonomy was restored via Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith.
homepage.agri_desc_full: Approximately 75% of the municipality's 30 km² is dedicated to lowland crop production, livestock, and poultry farming.
homepage.sources_desc: Much of Mapandan's historical material comes from the Municipality of Mapandan's official website, including the Municipal Profile, Physical Characteristics, and individual barangay history pages. Population data is from the Philippine Statistics Authority. Development milestones reference the Philippine News Agency and Department of Budget and Management records.

legislative.legal_basis_desc: The Municipality of Mapandan operates under Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991), situated within the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan. The Sangguniang Bayan — a unicameral local legislative council — exercises municipal legislative power, presided by the Municipal Vice Mayor and composed of elected councilors alongside ex-officio representatives from the Liga ng mga Barangay and the Sangguniang Kabataan Federation.

CY 2024 figures are the most recent actuals; CY 2025–2026 figures are SP-approved appropriations. transparency.credit_desc: Mapandan utilizes credit financing through state banks for capital expansion projects, leveraging future budget cycles to fund infrastructure modernization.

transparency.budget_2026_desc: SP Res. No. 438-2026, approved December 2025, authorizes the Annual General Appropriations for CY 2026.

transparency.budget_trend_note: Note about CY 2022 spike: Reflects one-time infrastructure transfers and supplemental appropriations.
transparency.fiscal_structure_desc: Mapandan's fiscal architecture relies heavily on intergovernmental transfers, with statutory earmarks limiting discretionary spending.
transparency.fiscal_nta_desc: Of total operating revenue, the majority comes from National Tax Allotment (NTA) formerly known as IRA.
transparency.fiscal_dev_fund_desc: Of annual NTA share, at least 20% is allocated to the Local Development Fund as mandated by R.A. 7160.

about.project_desc: Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal that compiles public data about the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan, into a single accessible platform. It is built and maintained by volunteers, not affiliated with the local government.
about.project_mission_desc: To make local government data accessible, understandable, and actionable for every resident of Mapandan, empowering informed civic participation.
about.project_how_desc: Data is gathered from official government sources such as COA reports, PSA censuses, SP resolutions, and municipal disclosures. Volunteers compile, verify, and present this information in a user-friendly format.
about.project_open_source_desc: The source code for Better Mapandan is publicly available on GitHub, allowing anyone to audit, contribute, or fork the project.
about.project_independent_desc: Better Mapandan operates independently of any government entity. It is a civic initiative run entirely by volunteers.
about.project_volunteer_desc: All data compilation, verification, and platform maintenance are performed by volunteer contributors from the community.
about.contribute_get_involved_desc: Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. There are many ways to help improve the portal.
about.contribute_report_desc: Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting incorrect or outdated information.
about.contribute_code_desc: Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve the platform by submitting pull requests on GitHub.
about.contribute_verify_desc: Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official documents and publications.
about.contribute_share_desc: Spread the word about Better Mapandan so that more residents can access their local government data.
about.disclaimer_desc: Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to the Municipal Government of Mapandan or any government agency. All data presented is compiled from publicly available official sources and is provided for informational purposes only.
